Q: Clojure - named arguments A:

Clojure 1.11 update

Updating on @Ryane 's answer with the newer capabilities of Clojure.

You can pass a map to a clojure function and all the de-structuring stuff are available in function signature (defaults using :or, binding using :as, etc.)

user=> (defn blah [{:keys [key1 key2 key3]}] (str key1 key2 key3))
user=> (blah {:key1 "I'm " :key2 "saying " :key3 "BLAH!"})
"I'm saying BLAH!"
user=> (blah {:key1 "I'm " :key2 "saying."})
"I'm saying."

You can even destructure a map within a map and so on!

user=> (defn we-has-maps [{:keys [foo bar] {:keys [a b]} :baz}] (str foo bar a b))
#'user/we-has-maps
user=> (we-has-maps {:foo "AAA" :bar "BBB" :baz {:a "CCC" :b "DDD"}})
"AAABBBCCCDDD"

If you want your function to be callable both like (my-fun :a 1 :b 2) and (my-fun {:a 1 :b 2}) you can add & before :keys (don't do this unless you have to.) example

Of course you can still use the old methods and styles, but it's discouraged.

Differentiating required params vs. optional params

There are two main common styles that I know of.

If there are a couple of required params and multiple optional params, we can make it so the function is called as (my-func true "x" {:opt1 "foo" :opt2 "bar"}), by defining the function as such:

(defn my-func [req1 req2 {:keys [opt1 opt2]}] ...)

This is a very clear signature and it's both obvious to the functions' consumer what are required and what are optional, and is enforced by the compiler and language itself.

Another method for more beefy functions is to only take a map (named params) and specify required and optional params in the docstring (So the consumer can clearly see, without reading the function's definition), and checking the required params in a :pre condition (read about pre-conditions)

(defn my-unc 
  "My function that does something.

  * named args
    * REQ: req1 -- this does something critical
    * REQ: req2 -- this is because of xyz
    * opt1 -- You can do something with it
    * opt2 -- changes the color"
  [{:keys [req1 req2 opt1 opt2]}]
  {:pre [(and (some? req1) (string? req1))
         (seq? req2)]}
...)

Q: The application completed without reading the entire request body, .net core 2.1.1 A:

The error info of the application completed without reading the entire request body often occurs when the client send a request that doesn't fulfill the server requirements . In other words , it happens just before entering the action , resulting that you cannot debug it via a breakpoint within the body of action method .

For example , let's say a action method on the server :

[Route("api/[controller]")]
[ApiController]
public class DummyController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpPost]
    public DummyDto PostTest([FromBody] DummyDto dto)
    {
        return dto;
    }
}

The DummyDto here is a dummy class to hold information:

public class DummyDto 
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
}

When clients send a request with payload not well formatted

For example , the following post request , which doesn't have a Content-Type: application/json header :

POST https://localhost:44306/api/test HTTP/1.1
Accept : application/json

{ "id":5 }

will result in a similar error info :

Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Internal.WebHost:Information: Request starting HTTP/1.1 POST http://localhost:44306/api/test  10
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Internal.WebHost:Information: Request finished in 1.9319ms 404 
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel:Information: Connection id "0HLGH8R93RPUO", Request id "0HLGH8R93RPUO:00000002": the application completed without reading the entire request body.

and the response from the server will be 404:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Server: Kestrel
X-SourceFiles: =?UTF-8?B?RDpccmVwb3J0XDIwMThcOVw5LTFcU08uQXV0aFJlYWRpbmdXaXRob3V0RW50aXRlQm9keVxBcHBcQXBwXGFwaVx0ZXN0?=
X-Powered-By: ASP.NET
Date: Mon, 03 Sep 2018 02:42:53 GMT
Content-Length: 0

As for the question you described , I suggest you should check the following list :

  1. does the Postman send the request with a header of Content-Type: application/json ? make sure you have checked the header
  2. If step1 doesn't work , click the code to show what it sends exactly when you send a request to the server .

Q: Regrading Wildfly Console Management connection with Wildfly 37/39 A:

This looks like a WildFly 37+ Aesh/JANSI compatibility regression specific to Windows CMD. The NoSuchMethodError breaks terminal input, which explains why the SSL certificate prompt hangs, while Linux remains unaffected. Using the compatible Aesh version or -Dorg.jboss.as.cli.aesh.terminal=dumb is a reasonable workaround until the dependency mismatch is fixed upstream.

Q: "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '...' even though module is installed A:

The problem was that in Visual Studio Code, sys.path showed python38-32, but the module was installed in python39. To fix the issue, go to menu View → Command Palette → Select Interpreter, and make sure to use the version under which pip installed the module.

This answered my question: How can I change the Python version in Visual Studio Code?
